quote: Human brains don't have smart juice.
tension: You'd never say you believe in it. But you check the gauge every time something gets hard.
situation: We talk as if every brain ships with a fixed ration of *mental horsepower*, doled out at birth. "She's so bright." "He doesn't have the horsepower." "I'm just not smart enough for this." You never pictured a fluid, but that's the *model you've been running*.
principle: Watch what the model does with struggle: hit something hard, feel the strain, and the needle reads *near empty*. But no one has ever found the juice. It belongs with the humors and phlogiston, invisible substances invented to explain what we couldn't yet see, *gone the moment we could*.
brain: Open up a brain and there is no tank to read. There are *networks built through learning*, refined by practice until they run on their own. What we call intelligence is what those networks have *learned to do*. Nothing to have more or less of.
reframe: So the strain of a hard problem was never your reserve draining. It was *wiring being built*. You're not running low. You're *under construction*.
ctaPunch: You weren't issued a ration. You're *building the whole thing*.
